intent_en: To demonstrate that high-income earners face a higher effective tax rate than the ultra-wealthy, and that the ultra-wealthy's tax burden has decreased since 2001.
previous_intent: To compare the effective tax rates between the wealthiest individuals and upper-middle-income earners, highlighting that the richest paid a lower rate in the later year than the higher-earning bracket and that their tax burden decreased from the earlier year.
narration_support: If you earn between $100,000 and $200,000, you will be paying up to 25% effective tax rate... The 400 richest tax returns surveyed by the IRS paid just 18.1% in 2008... In 2001... that rate was 23%.
chart_support: Bar chart comparing 2008 effective tax rates for the '400 richest' (18.1%) and '$100,000 - $200,000' (25%) groups, with a 2001 rate of 23% for the richest group, showing the richest pay less than the higher income bracket and their rate has dropped.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly compares the 25% rate for the $100k-$200k bracket with the 18.1% rate for the top 400 in 2008 (down from 23% in 2001). The chart visualizes this with bars showing 25% > 18.1% and a historical marker for 23%.
